Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase as the umpires make their way to the middle followed by the players of Sri Lanka who spread to their respective field positions. Tinashe Kamunhukamwe and Craig Ervine are the openers for Zimbabwe while Dilshan Madushanka will bowl the first over.
... RUN CHASE ...

Zimbabwe bowled brilliantly in the first phase of the game but an expensive 15th over that leaked 18 runs broke the shackles for Lanka as they managed to score 90 off the last 6 overs. Blessing Muzarabani and Luke Jongwe got a couple each while Wellington Masakadza and Richard Ngarava chipped in with one apiece. The target is a good one but the surface would get better to bat on under lights. Let's see if the Zimbabweans can chase this down with the second essay coming up shortly.

After being asked to bat, The Lankan innings started poorly as they lost 4 wickets in the powerplay and managed to score just 31 off the first 6 overs. The wicket was good to bat on but poor shot selection caused havoc in the Lankan camp as they lost wickets in a jiffy. The side was urging for a stable partnership which was given by Charith Asalanka and Angelo Mathews as they managed to put together 118 runs for the 5th wicket. The duo could have done better with frequent strike rotations but they made good ground for it thanks to a brilliant knock by Charith Asalanka as he got his 5th half-century in T20I and scored 69 off 39. Angelo Mathews took his time to get going but accelerated at the right moment and scored 66 at a strike rate of nearly 130.
A late surge extracting 90 runs of the last 6 helps the Lanks post 173 on board. A brilliant recovery from the Lankans to post 173 after being 4 down on just 27.

Dot to end the innings! Blessing Muzarabani bangs it short and around off. Wanindu Hasaranga looks to play the upper cut but fails to connect. Sri Lanka finishes on 173 for 6. Great recovery by the home side after they were reduced to 27 for 4.

Commentary.Commentary: We are live as the umpires walk to the middle followed by the players of Zimbabwe. Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis are the openers while Richard Ngarava will bowl the first over.

Skipper of Sri Lanka Wanindu Hasaranga says they were thinking of batting first only so happy with the toss. Adds that the batters need to take the responsibility and they shall post a good total here. Adds that everybody knows the importance of Angelo Mathews and they would be counting on him again as he has been a great servant of the nation for long. Informs Dilshan Madushanka comes in for Nuwan Thushara

Skipper of Zimbabwe Sikandar Raza has won the toss and he has decided to BOWL first. He says the wicket doesn't look too hard and it looks like a two-paced wicket and it might get worse before getting better. Adds that they ideally will look to bowl better on this track. Mentions that Sean Williams is fit for this game and they are going in unchanged.

Zimbabwe (Unchanged Playing XI) - Craig Ervine, Tinashe Kamunhukamwe, Brian Bennett, Sean Williams, Sikandar Raza(C), Ryan Burl, Clive Madande(WK), Luke Jongwe, Wellington Masakadza, Blessing Muzarabani, Richard Ngarava.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis(WK), Kusal Perera, Sadeera Samarawickrama, Charith Asalanka, Angelo Mathews, Wanindu Hasaranga(C), Dasun Shanaka, Dushmantha Chameera, Maheesh Theekshana, Dilshan Madushanka (in place of Nuwan Thushara).
TOSS UPDATE - Zimbabwe have won the toss and opted to BOWL first.

The visitors on the other hand had a good game with the ball but they leaked away way too many in the last 6 overs costing them the game. The side needs to work on finding the best form of their batters as they were in absolute shambles in the first game. Apart from skipper Sikandar Raza, no batter could put up a significant performance with the willow which meant they scored under par. The side is still looking for the best combination and they would require some senior pals to buckle up this time. Will the Lankans seal the deal or do the Zimbabweans level the series? Let's find out with toss and team updates in a while.

The hosts managed to get over the line on the last ball of the game in the previous encounter thanks to a solid partnership between Dasun Shanaka and Angelo Mathews and a couple of lusty hits from Dushmantha Chameera right at the end. The Lankans bowled brilliantly and only Sikandar Raza managed to put up some fight with the bat against them but the hosts need to work on their batting right at the top as they were lagging in the game for the majority of the run chase.

Hello and welcome to everyone tuning in as we build up to match number 2 of the three-match T20I series between Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe. Just like the first game, R. Premadasa Stadium, Colombo will host this game as well.
…MATCHDAY…

It is time for the second T20I of the three-match series between Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe. The iconic R Premadasa Stadium in Colombo will be the setting again as Zimbabwe look to force a series decider, whereas Sri Lanka, fresh off a thrilling last-ball win, aim to seal the series with a game to go. In the series opener, the experienced pair of Angelo Mathews and Dasun Shanaka bailed Sri Lanka out of trouble before Dushmantha Chameera finished it. However, it was all set up by their bowling unit, which restricted Zimbabwe to 143. The spin twins Maheesh Theekshana and Wanindu Hasaranga spun a web around the Zimbabwean batters, whereas the seam duo of Nuwan Thushara and Dushmantha Chameera were expensive. The newly appointed T20I skipper Wanindu Hasaranga and the team management will be disappointed with the batting display from the top five batters, despite the win. Kusal Mendis, Kusal Perera, and Charith Asalanka got starts but failed to kick on, and the trio would want to make their starts count in this game. For Zimbabwe, it was their captain, Sikandar Raza, who led the way with both bat and ball but it was not enough on the night. Despite wickets falling around him, Raza held one end and gave his bowlers something to defend with a 62-run knock. The Zimbabwean bowlers gave a good account of themselves and had Sri Lanka on the ropes at 84-6. However, they let the hosts off the hook and were just not able to hold their nerves when it mattered the most. The Chevrons came close to winning their first-ever T20I against the Asian side, but they would have taken plenty of positives from that game. Craig Ervine, Sean Williams, and Ryan Burl failed to have any impact of sorts with the bat, and as the visitors look to level the series, this trio will have to step up and get the runs. Whether it was the second ODI or the first T20I, the Zimbabwean bowlers haven't quite been able to nail their lines and lengths in pressure situations, and that is an aspect they would want to improve on. Will Zimbabwe hit back and take the series to a decider? Or will it be Sri Lanka to wrap up the series? Whatever happens, one thing is sure, we are in for an entertaining contest.
